g.text: Labeled arrows: learned weights. Unlabeled arrows: information flow. Biases are listed with their outputs.
A Encode current predictors and concatenate their representations
Recency; item age; prior mean spacing; spacing-availability flag
Student logitdec; student-item logitdec; student-item PPES
Current predictors x(t): concatenate 32 numeric + 16 item + 16 skill = 64 values
Item embedding: 16 values per item, initialized at zero; skill-combination embedding: 16 values, random start
Both tables train; reserved rows stay zero. Apply input dropout 0.1 after concatenation.
Carry exact raw item and skill-combination IDs alongside x(t).
B Retrieve completed memories: one attention head, width 32
Carry raw item/skill IDs alongside e(t).
Past completed events from this participant; newest 100 globally
Stored e(j): 96, post-answer h3(j): 32, exact raw item/skill IDs
FILTER: past item = current item OR past skill-combination ID = current ID
Attention and weighted mean m(t): 32 values
Current q(t) and past k(j): shared Linear 96 → 32; 32 shared biases
Scores q(t) · k(j) / sqrt(32); softmax over eligible past events only
Weighted mean Σ a(t,j) h3(j) of their raw post-answer states; no separate value map
* Q/K map shared: 3,072 weights + 32 biases (count once).
No attention decay or attention dropout.
C Predict the current response; the answer is still unknown
Correctness probability p(correct at trial t)
D Observe the answer, update all three layers, then store the completed event
Retain all three states h1(t), h2(t), h3(t) for the next trial
Append [cached pre-answer e(t): 96, post-answer h3(t): 32, raw item/skill IDs] to the bank
Keep the newest 100 global completed events; retained GRU states are before between-layer dropout.
Unlabeled arrows pass information; dashed arrows carry state or bank records to the next trial. Crossings without dots are not joins.
I and S are learned category counts. Training-only scaling/vocabularies; dropout off for evaluation; new participants start with zero states and an empty bank.
